name: Bacterial Wilt
description: A devastating bacterial disease affecting garden egg and other solanaceous crops. The bacteria invade the vascular system, blocking water transport and causing sudden wilting. It is most severe in warm, wet conditions and can persist in soil for years.
symptoms: Sudden wilting of leaves starting with lower leaves
Leaves turning yellow then brown without spotting
Brown discoloration inside the stem when cut
White bacterial ooze from cut stems placed in water
Plant collapsing and dying within days
causes: Bacteria surviving in contaminated soil for years
Root damage from cultivation or nematodes
Warm temperatures (25-35°C) with high soil moisture
treatments: Remove and burn infected plants immediately
Apply copper-based bactericide as soil drench
No curative treatment — focus on prevention
Solarize soil by covering with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks
prevention: Use disease-free seedlings from reputable nurseries
Practice long crop rotation (3-4 years) with non-solanaceous crops
Avoid damaging roots during transplanting and weeding
Improve drainage to reduce soil moisture
Graft susceptible varieties onto resistant rootstocks
